result.title: UMAMI: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Evidence-Grounded Dietary Decisions
result.comment: 40 pages, 15 figures, 16 tables. Dataset, code, and dashboard: https://umami-benchmark.github.io
result.summary: Dietary decisions require identifying a food's nutrient content and considering individual dietary needs, but recognizing food from an image alone does not provide this information. Visually similar foods can have different nutrient profiles, so selecting the wrong food record can lead to incorrect decisions even when nutrient rules are applied correctly. Furthermore, satisfying nutrient constraints does not necessarily establish a food's relevance to a person's intake. Evaluating these challenges together requires connecting food images, nutrient records, and individual intake histories. To support this evaluation, we introduce UMAMI (Unified Multimodal Assessment of Meals and Intake), a multimodal dataset and benchmark linking independently collected food images with nutrient profiles and respondent health and intake records. Using this dataset, we construct three diagnostic tasks covering visual nutrient question answering, personalized food recommendation, and condition-aware food substitution. Paired instances and input controls examine how visual identity and respondent context affect decisions. Our experiments identify errors in both food-record selection and nutrient-rule application, while showing that higher rule compliance does not necessarily improve alignment with subsequent recorded intake. These findings highlight the need to evaluate how multimodal systems select and use structured evidence for dietary decisions. The dataset, code, and dashboard are available at https://umami-benchmark.github.io.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 UMAMI 多模态数据集与基准，将食物图像与营养档案、个体摄入记录关联，并设计视觉营养问答、个性化推荐和情境感知替代三项诊断任务，用配对样本和输入控制检验视觉身份与用户情境对决策的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其区分食物记录选择错误与营养规则应用错误，并检验「遵守规则未必对齐真实摄入」，可为 VLM 如何筛选并真正使用视觉与结构化证据提供评测思路；但属特定应用领域，与 latent 推理状态生成机制联系有限，任务设计能否迁移仍需核查。
